sanskrit: anādyaṃ yat paraṃ brahma na devā narṣayo viduḥ ekas tad veda bhagavān dhātā nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
english: That supreme Brahman, which is without beginning, neither the gods nor the seers comprehend; the Lord Nārāyaṇa alone, the Ordainer, the Sovereign, knows it.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇād ṛṣigaṇās tathā mukhyāḥ surāsurāḥ rājarṣayaḥ purāṇāś ca paramaṃ duḥkhabheṣajam
english: From Nārāyaṇa the hosts of seers, the foremost gods and demons, and the royal sages of old received that supreme remedy for sorrow.

sanskrit: puruṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ bhāvaṃ prakṛtiḥ sūyate sadā hetuyuktam ataḥ sarvaṃ jagat saṃparivartate
english: Presided over by the Person, Nature ever brings forth existence; bound up with cause, the whole world thereby revolves on.

sanskrit: dīpād anye yathā dīpāḥ pravartante sahasraśaḥ prakṛtiḥ sṛjate tadvad ānantyān nāpacīyate
english: As from one lamp other lamps are kindled by the thousands, so Nature creates, yet, being infinite, is never diminished.

sanskrit: avyaktakarmajā buddhir ahaṃkāraṃ prasūyate ākāśaṃ cāpy ahaṃkārād vāyur ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ
english: From the Unmanifest, born of action, arises the intellect; the intellect brings forth the I-sense; from the I-sense comes ether, and from ether arises wind.

sanskrit: vāyos tejas tataś cāpas tv adbhyo hi vasudhodgatā mūlaprakṛtayo 'ṣṭau tā jagad etāsv avasthitam
english: From wind comes fire, from fire the waters, and from the waters the earth springs up; these are the eight root-natures, and in them the world abides.

sanskrit: jñānendriyāṇy ataḥ pañca pañca karmendriyāṇy api viṣayāḥ pañca caikaṃ ca vikāre ṣoḍaśaṃ manaḥ
english: From these come the five organs of knowledge, the five organs of action, and the five objects of sense; and the mind is the one and sixteenth among the modifications.

sanskrit: śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā ghrāṇaṃ pañcendriyāṇy api pādau pāyur upasthaś ca hastau vāk karmaṇām api
english: Ear, skin, the two eyes, tongue, and nose—these are the five sense-organs; and the feet, the anus, the generative organ, the two hands, and speech are the organs of action.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśo 'tha rūpaṃ ca raso gandhas tathaiva ca vijñeyaṃ vyāpakaṃ cittaṃ teṣu sarvagataṃ manaḥ
english: Sound, touch, then form, taste, and likewise smell—these are to be known; and the pervading consciousness, the mind, is present in all of them.

sanskrit: rasajñāne tu jihveyaṃ vyāhṛte vāk tathaiva ca indriyair vividhair yuktaṃ sarvaṃ vyastaṃ manas tathā
english: In the knowledge of taste it is the tongue, and likewise speech in utterance; joined with the manifold organs, the mind is distributed throughout them all.

sanskrit: vidyāt tu ṣoḍaśaitāni daivatāni vibhāgaśaḥ deheṣu jñānakartāram upāsīnam upāsate
english: One should know these sixteen divinities each in its own division; in the bodies they wait upon and worship the Knower, the maker of knowledge, seated within.

sanskrit: tadvat somaguṇā jihvā gandhas tu pṛthivīguṇaḥ śrotraṃ śabdaguṇaṃ caiva cakṣur agner guṇas tathā sparśaṃ vāyuguṇaṃ vidyāt sarvabhūteṣu sarvadā
english: Thus the tongue has the quality of Soma, and smell is the quality of earth; the ear has sound for its quality, and the eye is the quality of fire; and touch one should know as the quality of wind, in all beings and at all times.

sanskrit: manaḥ sattvaguṇaṃ prāhuḥ sattvam avyaktajaṃ tathā sarvabhūtātmabhūtasthaṃ tasmād budhyeta buddhimān
english: The mind, they say, has goodness for its quality, and goodness too is born of the Unmanifest, abiding as the self in all beings; therefore let the wise man understand it so.

sanskrit: ete bhāvā jagat sarvaṃ vahanti sacarācaram śritā virajasaṃ devaṃ yam āhuḥ paramaṃ padam
english: These existences bear up the whole world with all that moves and is unmoving, resting upon that passionless God whom they call the supreme abode.

sanskrit: navadvāraṃ puraṃ puṇyam etair bhāvaiḥ samanvitam vyāpya śete mahān ātmā tasmāt puruṣa ucyate
english: The holy city of nine gates, furnished with these existences, the great Self pervades and there reposes; and therefore is it called the Person who dwells in the city (puruṣa).

sanskrit: ajaraḥ so 'maraś caiva vyaktāvyaktopadeśavān vyāpakaḥ saguṇaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sarvabhūtaguṇāśrayaḥ
english: Ageless is He and deathless, expounded as both manifest and unmanifest, all-pervading, endowed with qualities, subtle, the support of the qualities of all beings.

sanskrit: yathā dīpaḥ prakāśātmā hrasvo vā yadi vā mahān jñānātmānaṃ tathā vidyāt puruṣaṃ sarvajantuṣu
english: As a lamp is luminous by nature, whether it be small or great, so should one know the Person, whose essence is knowledge, present in all creatures.

sanskrit: so 'tra vedayate vedyaṃ sa śṛṇoti sa paśyati kāraṇaṃ tasya deho 'yaṃ sa kartā sarvakarmaṇām
english: It is He who here knows what is to be known, He who hears, He who sees; this body is His instrument, and He is the doer of all actions.

sanskrit: agnir dārugato yadvad bhinne dārau na dṛśyate tathaivātmā śarīrastho yogenaivātra dṛśyate
english: As the fire latent in wood is not seen until the wood is split, so the Self abiding in the body is perceived here only through yoga.

sanskrit: nadīṣv āpo yathā yuktā yathā sūrye marīcayaḥ saṃtanvānā yathā yānti tathā dehāḥ śarīriṇām
english: As the waters are bound up in rivers, as the rays belong to the sun, streaming forth as they flow on, so are the bodies of embodied beings.

sanskrit: svapnayoge yathaivātmā pañcendriyasamāgataḥ deham utsṛjya vai yāti tathaivātropalabhyate
english: As in the state of dream the Self, gathered together with the five senses, casts off the body and wanders forth, even so is it to be apprehended here.

sanskrit: karmaṇā vyāpyate pūrvaṃ karmaṇā copapadyate karmaṇā nīyate 'nyatra svakṛtena balīyasā
english: By action it is first overspread, by action it comes into being, and by action—by the deeds it has wrought, mightier than all else—it is led elsewhere.

sanskrit: sa tu dehād yathā dehaṃ tyaktvānyaṃ pratipadyate tathā taṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi bhūtagrāmaṃ svakarmajam
english: And how, abandoning one body, it passes from body to body and takes on another—of this aggregate of beings, born of their own action, I shall now fully speak to you.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca caturvidhāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca avyaktaprabhavāny āhur avyaktanidhanāni ca avyaktanidhanaṃ vidyād avyaktātmātmakaṃ manaḥ
english: The teacher said: Beings are of four kinds, both unmoving and moving; they have the Unmanifest for their source and the Unmanifest for their dissolution, they say. Let one know that the mind, whose nature is dissolution into the Unmanifest, has the Unmanifest for its very self.

sanskrit: yathāśvatthakaṇīkāyām antarbhūto mahādrumaḥ niṣpanno dṛśyate vyaktam avyaktāt saṃbhavas tathā
english: As the mighty fig-tree, lying hidden within the tiny seed of the aśvattha, is seen to come forth full-grown, so does the manifest arise from the unmanifest.

sanskrit: abhidravaty ayaskāntamayo niścetanāv ubhau svabhāvahetujā bhāvā yadvad anyad apīdṛśam
english: The lodestone draws the iron toward itself, though both are without consciousness; even so existences arise from causes inherent in their own nature, and so too is it with whatever else is of this kind.

sanskrit: tadvad avyaktajā bhāvāḥ kartuḥ kāraṇalakṣaṇāḥ acetanāś cetayituḥ kāraṇād abhisaṃhitāḥ
english: Even so the existences born of the Unmanifest, marked as the instruments of the doer, though themselves unconscious, are bound together by cause for the sake of the conscious one.

sanskrit: na bhūḥ khaṃ dyaur na bhūtāni narṣayo na surāsurāḥ nānyad āsīd ṛte jīvam āsedur na tu saṃhitam
english: Neither earth nor space nor heaven, neither the elements nor the seers, neither gods nor demons, nor anything else existed apart from the living soul; nor had they yet come together in combination.

sanskrit: sarvanītyā sarvagataṃ manohetu salakṣaṇam ajñānakarma nirdiṣṭam etat kāraṇalakṣaṇam
english: By every reckoning it is all-pervading, having mind for its cause and bearing its own mark; the action of ignorance is what is pointed to here—this is the character of the cause.

sanskrit: tat kāraṇair hi saṃyuktaṃ kāryasaṃgrahakārakam yenaitad vartate cakram anādinidhanaṃ mahat
english: Conjoined with its causes, it is the gatherer-together of effects, by which this great wheel, without beginning or end, turns on.

sanskrit: avyaktanābhaṃ vyaktāraṃ vikāraparimaṇḍalam kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitaṃ cakraṃ snigdhākṣaṃ vartate dhruvam
english: The wheel whose hub is the Unmanifest, whose spokes are the manifest, whose rim is the round of modifications, presided over by the Knower of the field, turning upon a well-oiled axle, revolves unceasingly.

sanskrit: snigdhatvāt tilavat sarvaṃ cakre 'smin pīḍyate jagat tilapīḍair ivākramya bhogair ajñānasaṃbhavaiḥ
english: Because of its oiliness the whole world is crushed in this wheel like sesame, pressed down, as it were, by oil-pressers, by enjoyments born of ignorance.

sanskrit: karma tat kurute tarṣād ahaṃkāraparigraham kāryakāraṇasaṃyoge sa hetur upapāditaḥ
english: Out of craving, action lays hold of the I-sense as its possession; in the conjunction of cause and effect that craving has been shown to be the determining ground.

sanskrit: nātyeti kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ na kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā kāryāṇāṃ tūpakaraṇe kālo bhavati hetumān
english: The effect does not surpass its cause, nor the cause its effect; but in the bringing-about of effects, time becomes the operative ground.

sanskrit: hetuyuktāḥ prakṛtayo vikārāś ca parasparam anyonyam abhivartante puruṣādhiṣṭhitāḥ sadā
english: Joined to their causes, the primary natures and the modifications move toward one another, each upon each, ever presided over by the Person.

sanskrit: sarajas tāmasair bhāvaiś cyuto hetubalānvitaḥ kṣetrajñam evānuyāti pāṃsur vāterito yathā na ca taiḥ spṛśyate bhāvo na te tena mahātmanā
english: Fallen away through existences full of passion and darkness, driven on by the force of causes, it follows after the Knower of the field, as dust is borne along by the wind; yet that essence is not touched by them, nor are they touched by that great Self.

sanskrit: sarajasko 'rajaskaś ca sa vai vāyur yathā bhavet tathaitad antaraṃ vidyāt kṣetrakṣetrajñayor budhaḥ abhyāsāt sa tathā yukto na gacchet prakṛtiṃ punaḥ
english: As the wind may be either laden with dust or free of dust, so let the wise man know the difference between the field and the Knower of the field; and being thus disciplined through practice, he would not return again to Nature.

sanskrit: saṃdeham etam utpannam acchinad bhagavān ṛṣiḥ tathā vārtāṃ samīkṣeta kṛtalakṣaṇasaṃmitām
english: This doubt, once it arose, the blessed seer cut away; and so let one regard the matter, weighed by the marks already established.

sanskrit: bījāny agnyupadagdhāni na rohanti yathā punaḥ jñānadagdhais tathā kleśair nātmā saṃbadhyate punaḥ
english: As seeds scorched by fire do not sprout again, so, with its afflictions burnt away by knowledge, the Self is not bound again.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca pravṛttilakṣaṇo dharmo yathāyam upapadyate teṣāṃ vijñānaniṣṭhānām anyat tattvaṃ na rocate
english: The teacher said: As for the dharma marked by engagement in action, how it comes to be observed—to those steadfast in true knowledge no other principle is pleasing than this.

sanskrit: durlabhā vedavidvāṃso vedokteṣu vyavasthitāḥ prayojanam atas tv atra mārgam icchanti saṃstutam
english: Rare are the knowers of the Veda who stand firm in what the Veda enjoins; and so, with an end in view, men here desire the path that is held in honor.

sanskrit: sadbhir ācaritatvāt tu vṛttam etad agarhitam iyaṃ sā buddhir anyeyaṃ yayā yāti parāṃ gatim
english: Because it has been practiced by the good, this conduct is beyond reproach; this is the one understanding, and there is that other by which one reaches the supreme goal.

sanskrit: śarīravān upādatte mohāt sarvaparigrahān kāmakrodhādibhir bhāvair yukto rājasatāmasaiḥ
english: The embodied being, out of delusion, takes on all possessions, beset by the impulses of desire, anger, and the rest, born of passion and darkness.

sanskrit: nāśuddham ācaret tasmād abhīpsan dehayāpanam karmaṇo vivaraṃ kurvan na lokān āpnuyāc chubhān
english: Therefore let him who seeks to sustain the body do nothing impure; for one who leaves an opening in his conduct would not attain the auspicious worlds.

sanskrit: lohayuktaṃ yathā hema vipakvaṃ na virājate tathāpakvakaṣāyākhyaṃ vijñānaṃ na prakāśate
english: As gold alloyed with base metal, even when refined, does not shine forth, so knowledge whose dross is unburnt away does not shine.

sanskrit: yaś cādharmaṃ caren mohāt kāmalobhāv anu plavan dharmyaṃ panthānam ākramya sānubandho vinaśyati
english: And he who, drifting after desire and greed, practices unrighteousness through delusion, though he has set foot upon the path of dharma, perishes together with all his kin.

sanskrit: śandādīn viṣayāṃs tasmād asaṃrāgād anuplavet krodhaharṣau viṣādaś ca jāyante hi parasparam
english: Therefore let him pass through the objects of sense—sound and the rest—without attachment; for anger, elation, and dejection arise one from another.

sanskrit: pañcabhūtātmake dehe sattvarājasatāmase kam abhiṣṭuvate cāyaṃ kaṃ vā krośati kiṃ vadet
english: In this body made of the five elements, compounded of goodness, passion, and darkness, whom does one praise, at whom does one rail, and what is there to say?

sanskrit: sparśarūparasādyeṣu saṅgaṃ gacchanti bāliśāḥ nāvagacchanty avijñānād ātmajaṃ pārthivaṃ guṇam
english: In touch, form, taste, and the rest the foolish form attachment; through want of discernment they do not grasp that the earthy quality is sprung from their own selves.

sanskrit: mṛnmayaṃ śaraṇaṃ yadvan mṛdaiva parilipyate pārthivo 'yaṃ tathā deho mṛdvikārair vilipyate
english: As a dwelling made of clay is plastered over with clay itself, so this earthen body is smeared over with the modifications of clay.

sanskrit: madhu tailaṃ payaḥ sarpir māṃsāni lavaṇaṃ guḍaḥ dhānyāni phalamūlāni mṛdvikārāḥ sahāmbhasā
english: Honey, oil, milk, clarified butter, flesh, salt, jaggery, grains, fruits and roots—these, together with water, are modifications of clay.

sanskrit: yadvat kāntāram ātiṣṭhan nautsukyaṃ samanuvrajet śramād āhāram ādadyād asvādv api hi yāpanam
english: As one who is crossing a wilderness should give way to no longing, but in his weariness take food merely to sustain himself, though it be unsavory—

sanskrit: tadvat saṃsārakāntāram ātiṣṭhañ śramatatparaḥ yātrārtham adyād āhāraṃ vyādhito bheṣajaṃ yathā
english: even so, crossing the wilderness of worldly existence, intent on his labor, let him take food only for the journey's sake, as a sick man takes medicine.

sanskrit: satyaśaucārjavatyāgair yaśasā vikrameṇa ca kṣāntyā dhṛtyā ca buddhyā ca manasā tapasaiva ca
english: By truth, purity, uprightness, and renunciation, by good repute and by valor, by patience, by steadfastness, by understanding, by the mind, and by austerity—

sanskrit: bhāvān sarvān yathāvṛttān saṃvaseta yathākramam śāntim icchann adīnātmā saṃyacched indriyāṇi ca
english: let him dwell among all states of being as they come, each in its due order; and desiring peace, with undejected soul, let him also restrain the senses.

sanskrit: sattvena rajasā caiva tamasā caiva mohitāḥ cakravat parivartante hy ajñānāj jantavo bhṛśam
english: Bewildered by goodness, by passion, and by darkness, creatures turn round and round as on a wheel, sorely, through ignorance.

sanskrit: tasmāt samyak parīkṣeta doṣān ajñānasaṃbhavān ajñānaprabhavaṃ nityam ahaṃkāraṃ parityajet
english: Therefore let him rightly examine the faults that spring from ignorance, and ever cast off the I-sense, which has ignorance for its source.

sanskrit: mahābhūtānīndriyāṇi guṇāḥ sattvaṃ rajas tamaḥ trailokyaṃ seśvaraṃ sarvam ahaṃkāre pratiṣṭhitam
english: The great elements, the senses, the qualities—goodness, passion, and darkness—and the threefold world with its Lord: all this is established upon the I-sense.

sanskrit: yatheha niyataṃ kālo darśayaty ārtavān guṇān tadvad bhūteṣv ahaṃkāraṃ vidyād bhūtapravartakam
english: As here time, in its fixed course, displays the marks of the seasons, so let one know the I-sense within beings to be the impeller of beings.

sanskrit: saṃmohakaṃ tamo vidyāt kṛṣṇam ajñānasaṃbhavam prītiduḥkhanibaddhāṃś ca samastāṃs trīn atho guṇān sattvasya rajasaś caiva tamasaś ca nibodha tān
english: Let one know darkness, the bewilderer, as black and sprung from ignorance; and learn now these three qualities together, bound up with pleasure and pain—those of goodness, of passion, and of darkness.

sanskrit: pramoho harṣajaḥ prītir asaṃdeho dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ etān sattvaguṇān vidyād imān rājasatāmasān
english: Lack of confusion, joy-born delight, freedom from doubt, steadfastness, and memory—these one should know as the qualities of goodness; and these others as belonging to passion and darkness:

sanskrit: kāmakrodhau pramādaś ca lobhamohau bhayaṃ klamaḥ viṣādaśokāv aratir mānadarpāv anāryatā
english: desire and anger, heedlessness, greed and delusion, fear and weariness, dejection and grief, discontent, pride and arrogance, and ignobility.

sanskrit: doṣāṇām evamādīnāṃ parīkṣya gurulāghavam vimṛśed ātmasaṃsthānām ekaikam anusaṃtatam
english: Having examined the gravity and lightness of such faults as these, which abide within the self, let him reflect on each one in turn, continuously.

sanskrit: śiṣya uvāca ke doṣā manasā tyaktāḥ ke buddhyā śithilīkṛtāḥ ke punaḥ punar āyānti ke mohād aphalā iva
english: The pupil said: Which faults are cast off by the mind, which are loosened by the understanding, which return again and again, and which, through delusion, are as if without fruit?

sanskrit: keṣāṃ balābalaṃ buddhyā hetubhir vimṛśed budhaḥ etat sarvaṃ samācakṣva yathā vidyām ahaṃ prabho
english: Of which should the wise man weigh the strength and weakness with the understanding, by reasoned grounds? Declare all this to me, O master, so that I may know it.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca doṣair mūlād avacchinnair viśuddhātmā vimucyate vināśayati saṃbhūtam ayasmayamayo yathā tathākṛtātmā sahajair doṣair naśyati rājasaiḥ
english: The teacher said: When the faults are cut off at the root, the purified soul is set free; as a thing of iron destroys what is brought against it, so too the unperfected soul perishes through the inborn faults that spring from passion.

sanskrit: rājasaṃ tāmasaṃ caiva śuddhātmākarmasaṃbhavam tat sarvaṃ dehināṃ bījaṃ sarvam ātmavataḥ samam
english: That which is of passion and that which is of darkness, arising from action—for the pure soul, all this is the seed of embodied beings, and for one who is master of himself it is all alike.

sanskrit: tasmād ātmavatā varjyaṃ rajaś ca tama eva ca rajastamobhyāṃ nirmuktaṃ sattvaṃ nirmalatām iyāt
english: Therefore by the self-possessed man both passion and darkness are to be shunned; goodness, set free from passion and darkness, would attain to stainlessness.

sanskrit: atha vā mantravad brūyur māṃsādānāṃ yajuṣkṛtam hetuḥ sa evānādāne śuddhadharmānupālane
english: Or else they might declare, in the manner of sacred formula, that the taking of flesh is sanctioned by the Yajus; that same ground holds also for not taking it, in the keeping of the pure dharma.

sanskrit: rajasā dharmayuktāni kāryāṇy api samāpnuyāt arthayuktāni cātyarthaṃ kāmān sarvāṃś ca sevate
english: Through passion one may accomplish even works conjoined with dharma and bound up exceedingly with gain; and one pursues all desires as well.

sanskrit: tamasā lobhayuktāni krodhajāni ca sevate hiṃsāvihārābhiratas tandrīnidrāsamanvitaḥ
english: Through darkness one pursues deeds joined to greed and born of anger, delighting in the sport of violence, beset by sloth and sleep.

sanskrit: sattvasthaḥ sāttvikān bhāvāñ śuddhān paśyati saṃśritaḥ sa dehī vimalaḥ śrīmāñ śuddho vidyāsamanvitaḥ
english: He who abides in goodness, taking refuge therein, beholds the pure states of goodness; that embodied one is stainless, glorious, pure, and endowed with knowledge.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca rajasā sādhyate mohas tamasā ca nararṣabha krodhalobhau bhayaṃ darpa eteṣāṃ sādhanāc chuciḥ
english: The teacher said: By passion and by darkness, O bull among men, delusion is wrought, and anger, greed, fear, and arrogance; by the conquering of these one becomes pure.

sanskrit: paramaṃ paramātmānaṃ devam akṣayam avyayam viṣṇum avyaktasaṃsthānaṃ viśante devasattamam
english: They enter into the supreme One, the Supreme Self, the imperishable, undecaying God, Viṣṇu, who abides in the Unmanifest, the best of the gods.

sanskrit: tasya māyāvidagdhāṅgā jñānabhraṣṭā nirāśiṣaḥ mānavā jñānasaṃmohāt tataḥ kāmaṃ prayānti vai
english: But men whose limbs are scorched by His illusion, fallen from knowledge, bereft of hope, through the bewildering of their knowledge thereupon pass on indeed to desire.

sanskrit: kāmāt krodham avāpyātha lobhamohau ca mānavāḥ mānadarpād ahaṃkāram ahaṃkārāt tataḥ kriyāḥ
english: From desire men attain to anger, and to greed and delusion; from pride and arrogance comes the I-sense, and from the I-sense thereupon come actions.

sanskrit: kriyābhiḥ snehasaṃbandhaḥ snehāc chokam anantaram sukhaduḥkhasamārambhāj janmājanmakṛtakṣaṇāḥ
english: From actions comes the bond of affection, and from affection follows sorrow forthwith; from the undertaking of pleasure and pain men are made fit for birth and rebirth.

sanskrit: janmato garbhavāsaṃ tu śukraśoṇitasaṃbhavam purīṣamūtravikledaśoṇitaprabhavāvilam
english: And from birth comes the dwelling in the womb, arising from seed and blood, foul with the oozings of dung and urine, sprung from blood.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇābhibhūtas tair baddhas tān evābhipariplavan saṃsāratantravāhinyas tatra budhyeta yoṣitaḥ
english: Overcome by craving, bound by these things and drifting after them, let one there understand women to be the bearers of the loom of worldly existence.

sanskrit: prakṛtyā kṣetrabhūtās tā narāḥ kṣetrajñalakṣaṇāḥ tasmād etā viśeṣeṇa naro 'tīyur vipaścitaḥ
english: By their nature they are as the field, while men bear the mark of the Knower of the field; therefore let the discerning man pass beyond these in particular.
